items.criterion: The report is one fenced code block. The block starts with an `ARGUE:` header and a ═ rule, and holds all the template sections in order.
CLAIMS gives each assertion of the text as a `[Cn]` line, numbered from C1 with no gaps. Each claim is one clause in plain English.
ANNOTATED TEXT gives the original text word for word. The only addition is a `[Cn]` tag immediately after each claim.
Each finding entry has the marker of its section and cites claim IDs. An empty section shows `none`.
The VERDICT line has the template form, and each count equals the number of entries in its section.
After the code block, one plain-prose sentence gives the most critical finding of the report.
Z3 runs on an encoding of this text, and CONTRADICTIONS gives exactly what the solver returned.
The skill writes the Z3 script to `_argue_check.py` in the working directory, and deletes the script after it reads the result.
CONTRADICTIONS gives the user each hard contradiction that follows from the text, and no false alarm.
The report finds the main practical problems of the text that are not hard contradictions. These are goals that pull against each other, and vague terms or unclear scope that can hide a conflict.
Each tension and ambiguity entry is specific to this text, is in the correct section and says why it is important. No entry is filler.
